text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Housing programmes, social funds and economic recovery will have priority in Bosnia's presentation to foreign donors in Brussels, Moslem-Croat federation Prime Minister Edhem Bicakcic says. Sarajevo canton will present a 345-million German-mark project.

- Bosnian President Alija Izetbegovic and co-chairman in Council of Ministers Haris Silajdzic call on Serbs from Sarajevo suburbs, who resettled in Brcko after their neighborhoods' handover to federation authorities in March 1996, to return to their homes.
- International community's High Representative to Bosnia Carl Bildt calls for session on Bosnian economy on January 12 following informational donors' conference in Brussels.

- Serb Republic sent 10 witnesses and lawyers to Rome, among them two U.S. lawyers, for upcoming session on Brcko arbitration, newspaper says and adds that Serbs did not send their arbitration panel member Vitomir Popovic.
- Dutch government is expected to approve donation for purchase of 1,000 cows to will be distributed in territory of Moslem-Croat federation, agriculture official says.
- Bosnian furniture factory Sipad due to sign contract with German company IMK Schieder for export of five million German marks worth of furniture, Sipad export director Resad Tahirovic says.
- Sarajevo business bank "Central banka" approves loans of up to 3,000 German marks to citizens, bank manager says.
- Sarajevo gas company begins charging citizens for gas supply from December 11, hoping to meet some of the debt accumulated throughout the last year to the Russian gas supplier, newspaper says.

- If Bosnia had no perspective, we would not be here; creating common institutions is sign that Bosnian people finally realised a joint state can and must be built, World Bank Sarajevo director Rory O'Sullivan says in interview.
